2608.07796.title: CliniCARE-Bench: Clinical Calibrated Audit of Medical Reasoning in EHR
2608.07796.paper_summary: Large language models perform strongly on medical knowledge benchmarks, but reliable clinical deployment requires agents to conduct defensible investigations over heterogeneous, longitudinal records: determining what evidence is needed, retrieving and reconciling structured and free-text data, grounding conclusions in verifiable evidence, and deferring cases that cannot be resolved reliably. We introduce CliniCARE-Bench (Clinical Calibrated Audit of Medical Reasoning in EHR), a benchmark for retrospective clinical audit: 25 clinician-validated scenarios instantiated as 750 patient-specific cases over real-patient-derived MIMIC-IV data. Systems investigate each case through a governed, logged tool environment for record retrieval, computation, and policy access, and return one of four verdicts---Yes, No, Indeterminate: Lack of Data, or Indeterminate: Medically Ambiguous---the last two separating missing evidence from residual medical ambiguity. Beyond verdict accuracy, we score patient-evidence and policy grounding, process adherence, calibrated abstention, reliability, and efficiency against case-level reference verdicts produced by independent multi-model adjudication and calibrated against Clinical Board review. Every retrieval, computation, and report is replayable, so the investigation trace is inspectable and scorable. To our knowledge, CliniCARE-Bench is the first deployment-oriented clinical-agent benchmark to jointly evaluate real longitudinal EHR investigation, claim-level evidence grounding, governing-policy use, process adherence, and calibrated abstention within a common patient-level adjudication framework. Across 16 agentic systems, four-way accuracy spans 65.3-76.1%, but raw accuracy overstates investigation quality. Defect-free accuracy, which credits a verdict only when correct and free of prohibited shortcuts, is 4.8-14.8 points lower and reorders the leaderboard.
2608.07796.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型在醫學知識基準上表現強勁，但可靠的臨床部署需要代理人對異質的長期記錄進行可辯護的調查：確定所需的證據，檢索和調和結構化和自由文本數據，將結論基於可驗證的證據，並推遲無法可靠解決的案例。<lb/>我們介紹 CliniCARE-Bench（電子健康記錄中的臨床校準醫學推理審計），這是一個回顧性臨床審計的基準：25 個經臨床醫生驗證的場景，具體化為 750 個基於真實病人來源的 MIMIC-IV 數據的患者特定案例。<lb/>系統通過一個受管控的、記錄的工具環境調查每個案例，以進行記錄檢索、計算和政策訪問，並返回四種裁決之一——是、否、無法判定：缺乏數據，或無法判定：醫學模糊——最後兩者將缺失的證據與剩餘的醫學模糊區分開來。<lb/>除了裁決準確性，我們還對患者證據和政策基礎、過程遵循、校準的自我克制、可靠性和效率進行打分，這些都是根據獨立的多模型裁決產生的案例級參考裁決進行校準的，並經過臨床委員會審查。<lb/>每次檢索、計算和報告都是可重播的，因此調查痕跡是可檢查和可打分的。<lb/>據我們所知，CliniCARE-Bench 是首個面向部署的臨床代理基準，旨在共同評估真實的長期電子健康記錄調查、索賠級證據基礎、治理政策使用、過程遵循和在共同的患者級裁決框架內的校準自我克制。<lb/>在 16 個代理系統中，四方準確率範圍為 65.3-76.1%，但原始準確率過高地反映了調查質量。<lb/>無缺陷準確率僅在正確且不使用禁止捷徑時給予裁決，這一數據低了 4.8-14.8 分，並重新排序了排行榜。
